text:
Mia Chen: Drafting a short runbook for synthesizing tenant health signals into a single actionable score + handoff steps. Focus: onboarding status, renewal risk, enablement coordination, and a simple customer-facing checklist. Also want explicit caching/batching/streaming guidance for CS-runbooks. LMK if I missed anything.

Arjun Patel: Love it. Can we scope to 3 layers: 1) real-time stream signals (errors, stream disconnects), 2) near-real-time aggregates (5m token throughput, failed calls), 3) daily health snapshots (activation %, NPS?). Each layer maps to different ops actions.

Sarah Nguyen: +1. Proposal for a compact health_score formula we can display in the UI and include in handoffs: 0-100 where <45 = at-risk, 45-70 = watch, 70+ = healthy. Simple weighted inputs so it's explainable to customers.

Frank O'Leary: Customer-facing checklist idea: "What we monitor (latency, prefill success, stream stability), what we do (prefill retry policy, batch sizing, circuit backoff), what you can do (reduce sequence length, enable caching TTL)." Keep it one A4.

Mia Chen: Good. Drafting the scoring weights — want to keep math simple so CS can justify score in a renewal convo. Suggest weights: activation_rate 40%, successful_calls% 30%, prefill_success% 20%, avg_response_latency_score 10%.

Sarah Nguyen: Example pseudo-code for reproducibility (include in runbook and ops playbook):

```
# health_score (0..100)
health = round(min(100, 
    0.4 * activation_rate_pct +
    0.3 * successful_calls_pct +
    0.2 * prefill_success_pct +
    0.1 * latency_score_pct
))
# interpret: <45 risk, 45-69 watch, >=70 healthy
```

Arjun Patel: Ops rules tied to signals (short bullets):
- stream_error_rate > 2% -> open an enablement ticket + increase prefill attempts
- sustained latency 95th > 1.5s -> recommend batch tuning (reduce batch_size or increase batch_timeout) and schedule a performance call
- prefill_success < 80% -> run targeted prefill trial (smaller batches, longer prefill window)

Frank O'Leary: For customer handoff add a one-click summary email template that contains: health_score, top-3 risk drivers, last 72h incident list, recommended quick wins. Template: "Hi <owner>, your current health score is 53 (watch). Top drivers: prefill 64%, stream_error 3.1%, latency 95p 1.7s. Quick wins: enable TTL caching for common prompts, reduce max token length from 4096->2048 for spikes."

Alexa (CS Bot): AUTOGEN: sample telemetry snippet for runbook inclusion:
```
{ "tenant": "acme-corp", "health_score": 53, "drivers": {"prefill_success": 64, "stream_err_pct": 3.1, "latency_95p_ms": 1700}, "timestamp": 1747659990 }
```

Sarah Nguyen: Feedback capture: include a 3-question post-handoff form we send 48h after changes: 1) Did prefill improve? (yes/no), 2) Any functional regressions? (free text), 3) Rate current experience (1-5). Store results as events to feed into the next health snapshot.

Mia Chen: Implementation notes for caching/batching/streaming guidance in the runbook (short and prescriptive):
- Caching: set TTLs per prompt template (default 24h), use prefix-based cache keys, avoid caching user-personalized content.
- Batching: start with conservative batch_size=8 and batch_timeout=40ms; if latency SLO allows, grow to batch_size=32 and batch_timeout=100ms. Measure tail latency for adjustments.
- Streaming: prefer streaming for low-latency interactive UX but add a "graceful fallback": if stream disconnects, replay last stable token window + prefetched context.

Arjun Patel: Add failure-mode playbook snippets: when cache miss storm occurs, fallback to dedicated small pool or throttle new prefill jobs. Example command we include for SRE to kick off targeted prefill: `prefill-cli start --tenant acme-corp --batch-size 16 --window 2h`

Frank O'Leary: Can we add a one-pager for renewal conversations: score trend over 30/90 days, top persistent drivers, customer action checklist, suggested seat-of-support (concierge vs self-serve). Keeps renewal talk evidence-backed.

Mia Chen: I'll assemble a draft doc (1-page runbook + 1-page customer summary + ops snippets) this week. Who can review Thursday?

Sarah Nguyen: I can review Thursday morning.

Arjun Patel: I'll review and add the SRE commands and a small playbook for scaling prefill workers.

Frank O'Leary: I'll vet the customer-facing language and email template.

Alexa (CS Bot): Reminder scheduled: draft due Thursday 09:00 PST. :calendar:
